Title: A Chance to be Mentored Virtually by Academics Without Borders
NewsSubTitle: Academics Without Borders: virtual mentorship programme
NewsSummary: Aga Khan University's (AKU) President Mr Firoz Rasul formally launched the Virtual Faculty Mentorship Programme, an initiative of AKU's Network of Teaching and Learning on October 26, 2015.
NewsContent:
President Firoz Rasul formally launched a virtual Faculty Mentorship Programme that pairs mentors from Academics Without Borders with AKU faculty mentees drawn from medicine, nursing and education. AWB members from Canada and the US, and AKU faculty members from Kenya, Tanzania and Pakistan - 25 participants in all - joined the event online.

An initiative of AKU's Network of Teaching and Learning, the programme brings together mentor and mentee virtually for at least two years. AWB Mentors bring a rich experience in teaching, research and faculty development to this relationship.
 
"The mentor-mentee partnership is meant to prompt actionable research that will ultimately improve teaching practice, " Dr Tashmin Khamis, Director, TL_net, explained, "with the overall aim of enhancing scholarship of teaching and learning at AKU."
 
Mentors will support faculty members by collaboratively engaging in projects to enhance teaching and learning: providing assistance in publishing their work by co-writing, reviewing draft publications or identifying avenues of publication; and offering advice on relevant resources/links to further develop their scholarship in teaching and learning.

Steve Davis, Executive Director and Founder of AWB, lauded the successful partnership with AKU to date, and reiterated AWB's commitment to assisting AKU faculty members in the years ahead.

Expressing his appreciation and excitement at the launch of this initiative, President Rasul said: "Mentoring, coaching, and developing faculty, as all of you know, is a very important part of a university's role in building capacity for teaching and research. Without access to the type of experience that you all offer and bring, we would not be able to do the things we do."
